mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS below 1.5% is associated with negative 20-day returns in >55% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.2 percentage points over a 3-month period signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precede negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE rises >0.2pp in 3 months, the 20-day forward returns are positive in >45% of cases over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 250) and a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS <= 1.5) signals a stagflationary risk, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL > 250 and FEDFUNDS <= 1.5, the 20-day forward returns are positive in >45% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (defined by quarterly GDP growth > 2% annualized), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to overvaluation, leading to negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods of late-cycle expansion (GDP growth > 2% annualized), the 20-day forward returns are positive in >55% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105.0 within a month signals a contraction in the manufacturing sector, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO falls below 105.0 in a month, the 20-day forward returns are positive in >45% of cases over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 5% over a month signals robust consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST rises >5% in a month, the 20-day forward returns are negative in >45% of cases over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeding 0.5 percentage points within a month signals aggressive monetary tightening, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS rises >0.5pp in a month, the 5-day forward returns are positive in >45% of cases over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 250) and weak employment growth (PAYEMS growth < 0.5% in a month) signals a stagflationary risk, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 250 and PAYEMS growth < 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL > 250 and PAYEMS growth < 0.5% in a month, the 60-day forward returns are positive in >45% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.
